The id of the failed snippet to patch, as printed in that call's failure message. Send it only together with `edits`, and always use a valid editId that is referencing a failed execute call. Never send it alongside `input`.

When an execute call fails, ALWAYS retry with this instead of resending the snippet in `input`. Each edit replaces `find` with `replace` in the failed snippet, then the patched snippet re-runs from scratch. Edits apply in order: each `find` must match the snippet as already modified by the preceding edits. Requires `editId`; omit `input` when using it. If the patched snippet fails again, keep fixing it with further `edits` under the same editId - `find` must then match the already-patched snippet.
Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match.
Exact text in the failed snippet to replace. Must match exactly once unless `all` is true.
The JavaScript snippet to execute. Required unless `edits` is provided.

Thin grid lines and subtle contour marks on a fully transparent background. Line color `[accent.primary]` at 5–15% opacity. Stroke weight 0.5–1px. Uniform spacing at 20–40px intervals. Sparse and precise layout with clean intersections. No text, no labels, no filled shapes, no decorative elements. Output as a seamless overlay layer.

Sweeping ribbon-like translucent color bands curving and arcing in smooth continuous motions. Use 3–4 accent colors: `[accent.primary]`, `[accent.secondary]`, `[accent.tertiary]`, and optionally a fourth accent tone. Bands overlap with soft dissolving edges where they meet. Each ribbon at 70–90% opacity. Large scale composition cropped at the frame edges. Smooth arcs, no sharp corners. No text, no objects, no noise, no texture overlay. Output as a background fill layer.

A wide-format digital painting of an outdoor scene — a park or garden setting with [surface elements: grass, paths, trees, flowers] in the foreground, human figures at mid-distance engaged in casual activities [walking, reading, conversing], and [urban/architectural elements: buildings, bridges, skyline] visible in the soft-focus background. Color palette uses `[accent.primary]` for shadow tones, `[accent.secondary]` for vegetation and highlights, `[accent.tertiary]` for sky and atmospheric glow. Painterly brushwork, atmospheric perspective, warm directional lighting from one side. No text, no UI elements, no sharp digital edges.

A single [natural object: flower, plant, fruit, leaf] rendered in pixel art style on a transparent background. Use an 8x8 or 16x16 pixel grid per element. Color palette limited to 4-8 colors derived from `[accent.primary]`, `[accent.secondary]`, `[accent.tertiary]`, and their tints. Hard pixel edges, no anti-aliasing, no gradients within pixels. The object should be centered and clearly recognizable despite the low-resolution rendering style.

A set of simple pixel-art icons and geometric shapes on a transparent background, rendered in white at low opacity. Shapes include: small hearts, directional arrows, abstract cross patterns, simple star forms. Each shape is built from square pixels on an 8x8 or 16x16 grid. Scatter irregularly across a wide canvas with generous spacing. No gradients, no anti-aliasing, sharp pixel edges only.

Thin geometric arcs and straight measurement guide lines with small annotation tick marks on a fully transparent background. Monochrome line color `[accent.primary]` at 10–20% opacity. Stroke weight under 1px. Sparse, asymmetric placement with generous empty space between marks. No text, no labels, no filled shapes, no heavy grids. Output as a seamless overlay layer.
